project_roadmap_ref.concern: Correction-Aware Learning Gate: outcome, prior rejected-classifier evidence, and reassessment contract

objective: A Claude Code or Codex agent that leaves a self-noticed or user-flagged correction unrecorded is prevented from ending its turn until it either records the correction through the learned skill or successfully contests the finding, without requiring a new user message to force a retry.
audience_or_actor: Brian, as sole operator of the personal agent ecosystem, and every Claude Code/Codex agent session working under enforced-planning-governed repos

current_state_ref.concern: Existing --correction-mode block path: reads a CorrectionAuditReceiptV1, hard-blocks the Stop event on status=correction_unresolved, tested, but left off by default because the classifier that would populate the receipt (correction_learning_audit.py) was rejected on real native-corpus recall/precision evidence (Plan #135) and has no way for the agent to contest a wrong verdict

desired_outcome: Turning on the existing correction-mode hard block no longer risks silently stalling a session on a wrong classifier verdict, because the blocked agent has a real path to either comply or be released after a successful contest, and this is proven end to end on at least one real recorded instance from an actual session.
success_or_readout: Pass: a synthetic and one real (or realistic replay) blocked-turn case each show (a) a genuine unresolved correction stays blocked until the learning is recorded, and (b) a genuine non-correction, once contested, is released without requiring the agent to fabricate an unwanted learning entry -- with no case requiring a human to manually intervene to unstick the session. Fail: any case where a correct contest is not released, or an incorrect contest is released, within the frozen test set.

evidence_target.claim: The correction-mode block-or-contest loop can run unattended on a real Stop event without a human clearing a stuck session

capability_ref.concern: Stop-event hard block on an unresolved-correction receipt

capability_adoptions.intended_consumer: Every Claude Code/Codex Stop event in a repo with this hook installed

adoption_proof.claim: The extended hook still blocks a genuine unresolved correction and now also accepts a resolving contest verdict

capability_ref.concern: LLM-based correction classifier over transcript exchanges, rejected for autonomous blocking use on native-corpus recall/precision evidence

capability_adoptions.intended_consumer: The new contest-adjudication step: re-runs classification specifically on the agent's rebuttal text, not on raw multi-turn transcript

adoption_proof.claim: Re-judging one bounded rebuttal exchange achieves materially better precision/recall than the rejected whole-transcript classifier, on a frozen held-out set

capability_ref.concern: Durable cross-client coordination messages: send/poll/status/acknowledge, addressed by session

capability_adoptions.intended_consumer: Optional: a durable record of the block reason and the agent's contest, visible outside the blocked turn itself

adoption_proof.claim: A block-and-contest exchange is durably recorded and pollable by another session or by Brian, not only visible inside the blocked turn's own transcript

required_capability_refs.concern: Stop-event hard block on an unresolved-correction receipt
LLM-based correction classifier over transcript exchanges, rejected for autonomous blocking use on native-corpus recall/precision evidence
Durable cross-client coordination messages: send/poll/status/acknowledge, addressed by session

target_ref.concern: Reassessment contract's stated human-decision triggers (precision threshold, per-audit budget)

typed_dependencies.condition: Brian has now supplied the human decision Plan #135's own reassessment contract required (accept a materially lower per-call precision bar because the contest path bounds the cost of a wrong call); this design must state that explicitly rather than silently reopening the same rejected bar

material_unknowns.question: Should the contest-adjudication re-check reuse the same model tier as the original classifier (Sonnet, per Plan #135's evidence), or is a materially more expensive/careful pass justified now that Brian has said he will pay for reliability, and what does that cost per blocked turn look like in practice?

What exact retry/loop bound prevents an agent and the reviewer from cycling indefinitely on a genuinely ambiguous case, and what happens when that bound is hit (escalate to Brian via the mailbox, or fail open)?
Exact new CorrectionAuditReceiptV1 status value(s) and fields needed to represent 'contested, accepted' versus 'contested, rejected, blocked again' distinctly from today's four-state enum

non_claims: This does not claim the underlying classifier's raw recall/precision has improved over Plan #135's measured numbers -- it claims the contest path makes those numbers tolerable for blocking use, which is a different claim
This does not claim readiness for Codex specifically without its own native-format replay, given Plan #135 measured materially worse Codex recall than Claude Code recall
non_goals: Reviving whole-transcript semantic classification as the sole detector; the mechanical/marker-based detection path for closing-format violations stays as-is and is out of scope here
Building a general-purpose agent-to-agent negotiation protocol beyond this one gate
